clue.text: Part-time ambassador, having to do housework, failed

parts.note: a bit is a part or piece
HE stands for His Excellency, the title of an ambassador
to dust is a household chore

explanation.surface: A diplomat working part-time is reduced to cleaning and has flopped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Part-time' reads as one idea but splits in two; His (or Her) Excellency is the form of address for an ambassador.
explanation.definitionFit: To bite the dust is an idiom for collapsing or coming to grief, so 'failed' fits the past tense.

clue.text: Snack bar's offering primarily beans and pork sausages

indicators.note: primarily asks for the opening letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: A cafe's menu item leads with beans and pork sausages.
explanation.walkthrough: BAPS are soft bread rolls, a British staple of snack bars, often filled with sausages.
explanation.definitionFit: A bap is a soft round bread roll, a typical item sold at a snack counter.

clue.text: Change of heart in right-wing city of old

indicators.note: the central letters of the word for right-wing are altered, here swapped round

parts.note: a Tory is a British Conservative, a right-winger

explanation.surface: A politician of the right turns, in a city long ago.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Change of heart in' swaps the two middle letters of TORY, OR becoming RO.
explanation.definitionFit: Troy is the ancient city besieged by the Greeks in Homer's Iliad.

clue.text: Achilles' aunt in play sees visions

indicators.note: in play suggests letters moving about freely, so the preceding words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A relative of the Greek hero, appearing in a drama, has prophetic visions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in play' rearranges ACHILLESAUNT.
explanation.definitionFit: To hallucinate is to perceive things that are not there, like imagined visions.

clue.text: Any number have a liking for sex

parts.note: to dig something is slang for liking it
IT is a coy old word for sex or sex appeal

explanation.surface: Someone's fondness for sex, apparently in any quantity.
explanation.definitionFit: Each numeral from 0 to 9 is a digit, so any single number can be one.

clue.text: Assault force becoming excited

parts.note: to set on someone is to attack them
edge means sharpness or force, as in words with an edge

explanation.surface: An attacking army grows agitated.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that sets you on edge makes you tense and agitated, a jittery kind of stirring up.

clue.text: Exchange of prisoners rejected

indicators.note: rejected means thrown back, so the word for prisoners runs the other way

parts.note: POWs are prisoners of war

explanation.surface: A proposed prisoner exchange is turned down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns POWS backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Swop is a variant spelling of swap, a trade or exchange.

clue.text: Clear standard breached by training policy proposals by government

parts.note: white can mean clear or blank, as in white wine or white light

indicators.note: breached by says the standard is broken into by the training

parts.note: par is the standard or norm
PE is physical education, training

explanation.surface: A clear norm is broken by a training scheme, in a government document.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breached by' signals the insertion; PE is the school abbreviation for physical education.
explanation.definitionFit: A white paper is a government report setting out proposed policy before legislation.

clue.text: Daughter invested in Italian china, apparently, for mum or dad?

indicators.note: invested in means put inside, so daughter goes into the phrase

parts.note: china is rhyming slang for mate (china plate), so an Italian one is a pal in Rome

explanation.surface: A daughter puts money into Italian porcelain for one of her parents.
explanation.walkthrough: China = mate is Cockney rhyming slang (china plate). 'mum or dad' are examples, each reading the same backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Mum and dad both read identically in either direction, the defining property of such words.

clue.text: Dissolute master joining ship that's changed sides

parts.note: a pro is a master or expert

indicators.note: sides here are right and left, so the right letter is swapped for the left one

parts.note: a frigate is a warship

explanation.surface: A dissipated captain joins a vessel that has defected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changed sides' swaps R (right) for L (left) in FRIGATE.
explanation.definitionFit: A profligate is recklessly extravagant or immoral, synonymous with dissolute living.

clue.text: Works poorly after end of term

indicators.note: after says the word for poorly comes behind the letter taken from term
end of asks for the final letter of the word term

parts.note: poorly means unwell, ill

explanation.surface: Something functions badly once the school term finishes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Works' looks like a verb but is the noun: a factory.
explanation.definitionFit: A mill is a factory or industrial plant, which is what works means as a noun.

clue.text: How old prisoner is transported, when one can agree to act

definitions.text: when one can agree to act

parts.note: a convict's years are the age of the con, CON being slang for a prisoner
transported means sent away, as convicts once were to Australia

explanation.surface: An elderly convict is shipped off.
explanation.definitionFit: The age of consent is the legal age from which a person may agree to sexual activity.

clue.text: Proposing eco-friendly links, to some extent?

parts.note: putting, as in putting a question, means proposing
green means environmentally friendly

explanation.surface: Suggesting environmentally sound connections.
explanation.walkthrough: Links is a golf course, especially a seaside one; a putting green is one part of it.
explanation.definitionFit: A putting green is the smooth turf round each hole, so it forms part of a golf course.

clue.text: Hitchcock film sure to follow interval

indicators.note: to follow places the word for sure after the interval

parts.note: a spell is a period or interval of time
bound means certain, as in bound to happen

explanation.surface: A Hitchcock movie is certain to come after the break.
explanation.definitionFit: Spellbound is a 1945 psychological thriller directed by Alfred Hitchcock.

clue.text: Doctor met diarist to make superficial complaint

indicators.note: to doctor is to tamper with, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A physician has seen a diary writer with a minor ailment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' is a verb here, rearranging METDIARIST; 'superficial' means on the surface of the body.
explanation.definitionFit: Dermatitis is inflammation of the skin, a complaint affecting the body's surface.

clue.text: Brewing empire's leading wine opened first

indicators.note: leading puts the rearranged letters in front of the wine
brewing means stirring up, so the letters are mixed

parts.note: the word empire is the fodder; its 's reads as is, a link to what follows
red is red wine

explanation.surface: A vast realm makes its foremost wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brewing' rearranges EMPIRE as PREMIE, which leads RED; the 's reads as 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A play or film premiered when it had its first public performance or showing.

clue.text: Rising when expected, I subsequently hit back

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means read upwards, so everything is reversed

parts.note: ETA is the estimated time of arrival, when someone is expected
later means afterwards, subsequently

explanation.surface: Getting up at the expected hour, I struck back afterwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rising' reverses ETAILATER, the whole sequence, as the answer reads upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To retaliate is to respond in kind to an attack, striking in return.

clue.text: Recalled part of Wagnerian opera being broadcast

indicators.note: Recalled says the hidden letters are read backwards
part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An extract from a Wagner opera is played again on the radio.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recalled' reverses RIANO, found across 'Wagnerian opera'.
explanation.definitionFit: A programme on air is going out live on radio or television.

clue.text: Secondary proposition from man docked on lunar module

indicators.note: in an across clue, on means placed after

parts.note: LEM is the Lunar Excursion Module of the Apollo missions

indicators.note: docked means cut short, so the last letter goes

explanation.surface: A curtailed astronaut docks with the moon lander.
explanation.walkthrough: 'docked' cuts the final letter off 'man'; 'on' in an across clue means placed after.
explanation.definitionFit: In logic a lemma is a subsidiary theorem proved to help establish a main one.

clue.text: Manchester ground not cameraman's last picture

indicators.note: ground means crushed and mixed up, and not says a letter is left out of the mix
last asks for the final letter of the cameraman

explanation.surface: At a Manchester football stadium, the cameraman's final shot was missed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ground not' rearranges MANCHESTER without N, the last letter of 'cameraman'; 'Manchester ground' looks like a stadium.
explanation.definitionFit: The Scream is Edvard Munch's famous expressionist painting of an anguished figure.

clue.text: Merlot best in mixed drinks

indicators.note: mixed, as in mixing drinks, says the preceding letters are shuffled

explanation.surface: The finest Merlot is put into cocktails.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mixed' rearranges MERLOTBESTIN; 'in' is fodder, not a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Bitter lemon is a fizzy lemon-flavoured mixer, so these are soft drinks.

clue.text: Dad chopping tree up for timber

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the result is read upwards
chopping means cutting into, so dad goes inside the tree

parts.note: the elm is a tree
pa is a familiar word for father

explanation.surface: Father felling a tree to provide wood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chopping' signals insertion, giving ELPAM, and 'up' turns that whole string upwards in this down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Maple is a hardwood used for furniture and flooring, so it is a kind of timber.

clue.text: Serving men very roughly

parts.note: OR, other ranks, are soldiers below officer rank
so means very, as in so good

explanation.surface: Waiters treat customers very harshly.
explanation.walkthrough: OR (other ranks) is the British military term for enlisted soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: Or so follows a figure to mean approximately, as in ten or so.

clue.text: Defence ultimately presented by bank employee

indicators.note: ultimately asks for the final letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: A legal defence is finally offered by a bank clerk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Defence' looks like the start of the pick but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A dyke is an embankment built to keep out the sea or floods, a protective barrier.

clue.text: Doing less than

definitions.meaning: what are you ...? asks what you are doing
... a number means no more than it

explanation.surface: Doing less than required.
explanation.definitionFit: Up to is an idiom for engaged in, and also means as many as, a maximum.

clue.text: Horse died — Sue admits boundless regret

indicators.note: admits means lets in, so the inner letters go inside

parts.note: to sue for something is to apply for it formally

indicators.note: boundless strips the outer letters off regret

explanation.surface: A horse is dead, and Sue confesses endless sorrow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sue' looks like a name but is the verb, as in suing for peace. 'admits' signals insertion and 'boundless' trims both ends of 'regret'.
explanation.definitionFit: A dapple grey is a horse with a grey coat marked by darker rounded patches.

clue.text: The necessary spot of sweetener in tonic

indicators.note: in places the spot of sweetener inside the tonic

parts.note: doh is the tonic, first note of the scale in tonic sol-fa

indicators.note: a spot of means a small bit, here the first letter

explanation.surface: A drop of sugar is all a tonic needs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tonic' looks like a drink but is the keynote, DOH.
explanation.definitionFit: Dosh is British slang for money, and the necessary is another slang term for cash.

clue.text: Plant grew further behind ditch

indicators.note: behind places the growth word after the ditch word

parts.note: to ditch is to abandon, desert
rose means increased, grew further

explanation.surface: A plant grew taller beyond a trench.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ditch' looks like a trench but is the verb 'abandon'.
explanation.definitionFit: The desert rose is a succulent shrub with pink flowers, native to arid regions.
